questions.question: In standard-cell ASIC physical design, why are unused or tied-off logic gate inputs connected to VDD or VSS through dedicated 'Tie-High' or 'Tie-Low' cells rather than directly wired to the power and ground rails?
options: To protect the delicate transistor gate oxide from voltage surges, antenna damage, and electrostatic discharge (ESD) spikes occurring on the power rails
To invert the input polarity dynamically during automated scan test modes and built-in self-tests
To reduce dynamic capacitive switching power caused by high-frequency rail bounce
To prevent thermal runaway by introducing active cooling diodes at standard-cell boundaries
To eliminate the need for multi-layer routing vias when connecting signals to the uppermost metal layers

questions.question: In shared-memory multi-core processors, why is a directory-based cache coherence protocol favored over a snooping-based coherence protocol as the core count scales to dozens or hundreds of cores?
options: Directory-based protocols avoid tracking dirty cache lines, completely eliminating the need for write-backs
Snooping requires broadcast communication across all nodes, which saturates interconnect bandwidth, whereas directories use targeted point-to-point messages
Directory-based protocols physically combine L1, L2, and L3 caches into a unified, single-cycle centralized SRAM structure
Snooping protocols cannot support the MESI or MOESI states, making them incompatible with multi-threaded operating systems
Directory-based protocols eliminate all read and write latency by predicting future memory accesses at compile time

questions.question: In synchronous digital integrated circuit design, why is a hold-time violation generally considered far more critical and catastrophic than a setup-time violation during post-silicon testing?
options: Hold-time violations permanently destroy the physical p-n junctions of flip-flops due to excessive thermal dissipation
Setup-time violations can be repaired via laser trimming, whereas hold-time violations require full wafer re-fabrication
Hold-time margins are independent of the clock period, meaning a hold violation cannot be resolved by reducing the operating clock frequency
Hold-time violations only occur in dynamic domino logic and can never be detected by Static Timing Analysis (STA)
Hold-time violations flip the logical polarity of routing interconnects, corrupting clock-tree buffers

questions.question: In modern out-of-order superscalar microarchitectures, what is the primary role of the Reorder Buffer (ROB)?
options: To statically sort instruction opcodes prior to decoding to optimize execution-unit scheduling
To physically store branch prediction history tables and calculate indirect jump target addresses
To map architectural register specifiers directly to hardware arithmetic logic units (ALUs)
To track in-flight instructions in strict program order so that architectural state updates and exceptions commit in-order
To act as a secondary instruction cache that holds decoded micro-operations for loop streams

questions.question: In deep-submicron physical design and power integrity analysis, what is the fundamental distinction between static IR drop and dynamic IR drop across a chip's Power Delivery Network (PDN)?
options: Static IR drop affects only signal interconnects, whereas dynamic IR drop affects only the clock distribution network
Static IR drop is caused entirely by wire inductance, whereas dynamic IR drop is caused solely by junction substrate leakage
Static IR drop occurs exclusively during chip power-up, whereas dynamic IR drop occurs only during thermal shutdown
Static IR drop is measured in analog I/O domains, whereas dynamic IR drop is confined strictly to embedded SRAM arrays

Static IR drop is driven by average DC current dissipation across parasitic wire resistance, whereas dynamic IR drop is caused by localized peak switching currents and L(di/dt) transient inductive effects
